title: Administrator: Data
company: Norton Rose Fulbright LLP - Agency - Permanent
description:
Practice Group / Department:

IT Regional - Project & Program Management - London

Job Description

Norton Rose Fulbright is a global law firm with more than 3,000 lawyers advising clients across locations in the United States, Europe, Canada, Latin America, Asia, Australia, Africa and the Middle East. We provide the world's preeminent corporations and financial institutions with a full business law service.

With over 50 offices and 7,000 employees worldwide, our culture is the thread that connects us, as well as our values of unity, quality and integrity. Our strategy and culture are connected - defined by shared ambition, global collaboration and a one-team mindset. We believe pioneering work happens when people are empowered to think beyond boundaries, explore new opportunities and grow through diverse experiences. Alongside the right skills and experience, we look for people who are innovative, commercially minded, and motivated by the impact of the work they do - ready to share in our ambition and help shape what comes next.

Because while individuals can do well, together we achieve something extraordinary.

The Role

The Finance Systems Team is responsible for supporting the core EMEA finance system (Aderant Sierra), including time, billing, expenses, vendors, tax and reporting. We are seeking a Data Administrator, with Aderant and Finance Operations experience, to join our EMEA team.

This is a key role in supporting the day-to-day function of the firm's EMEA finance systems and will provide essential assistance to finance operations and other data users, including senior stakeholders in the firm. This will include delivery of ongoing data monitoring and support for master data management, and data acquisition and preparation for a variety of business and operational stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
- User Support: support application users, and respond to queries and requests from fee earners, secretaries and finance operations staff for data changes, extracts and updates.
- Troubleshooting and Issue Resolution: monitor the health and performance of data systems, identify and resolve quality issues, bottlenecks and anomalies, and identify, analyse and resolve and other data-related problems, and minimise errors.
- Work with third party support providers, IT and finance operations to resolve logged issues.
- Data Monitoring and Management: support the provision of advanced data management for financial systems, including applying data governance and stewardship standards, supporting enforcement of permission structures, maintaining data taxonomies, schemas and mapping, conducting regular data cleansing, de-duplication and remediation, and updating and changing data in line with changing business needs.
- Data Acquisition and Preparation: source, collect, clean and structure data for operational use and analysis, using SQL queries and logic if necessary.
- Continuous Improvement: understand user requirements and requests, identify opportunities for enhancements and work with teams to test and implement changes.
- Help to improve procedures and processes for all stakeholders.

Skills and Experience Required

We are seeking a proactive, and solutions-oriented individual with experience working with financial systems and finance operations.

You will need to be able to communicate effectively with a range of stakeholders at all levels across the business, including for a variety of data and business intelligence issues and stakeholder requests.

You'll also need the following skills and experience:
- Ideally degree educated and/or 3+ years of experience a similar role.
- Good customer/user service abilities, demonstrated by resolving user queries and working with customers.
- Data management experience and/or expertise in finance practice management systems (FPMS).
- SQL proficiency, as well as the ability to run queries unsupervised.
- Experience working within structured ITSM frameworks, such as ITIL.
- Familiarity with core finance processes (general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, budgeting, forecasting, reporting) ideal.
- Experience within a law firm or other professional services environment desired.
- Solutions-orientated and proactive approach to work.
- Willingness to upskill on the job through internal and external training.
- Able to demonstrate discretion, sensitivity and confidentiality.
- Team player - flexible and willing to take on extra responsibilities to support departmental or firm objectives.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

To attract the best people, we strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone can bring their whole selves to work, have a sense of belonging, and realize their full career potential.
Our new enabled work model allows our people to have more flexibility in the way they choose to work from both the office and a remote location, while continuing to deliver the highest standards of service. We offer a range of family friendly and inclusive employment policies and provide access to programmes and services aimed at nurturing our people's health and overall wellbeing. Find more about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion here.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams. We strive to create an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates. If you require any tailored adjustments or accommodations, please let us know here.

title: HR Administrator

title: HR Assistant
description:
The Opportunity:
Temporary HR Assistant
- Location: South Tyneside
- Salary: £28,500 per annum, depending on skills, qualifications and HR experience
- Contract: Temporary, 2 to 3 months
- Hours: Monday to Friday, 9.00am to 5.00pm, 37.5 hours per week
- Working arrangement: Primarily office-based, with some home working potentially required depending on business needs

Are you an experienced HR Assistant looking for your next temporary opportunity?

My client is seeking a confident and proactive HR Assistant to provide comprehensive support across employee relations, recruitment, onboarding and HR administration. Reporting to the HR Manager, this is a varied role where you will work closely with managers across the business, offering first-line guidance and helping to deliver a professional, consistent and legally compliant HR service.

Key Responsibilities:
- Provide first-line HR advice to managers on attendance, probation, performance, conduct and other day-to-day employee relations matters.
- Support disciplinary, grievance, absence management, flexible working and capability processes.
- Prepare letters, meeting packs, scripts and other HR documentation tailored to individual cases.
- Take accurate notes during formal meetings and guide managers through company procedures.
- Support organisational change, restructures, redundancy consultations and TUPE-related administration.
- Assist with recruitment activity, including job descriptions, adverts, candidate communication and recruitment administration.
- Complete pre-employment checks, including right-to-work and DBS checks.
- Coordinate new starter administration, onboarding, inductions and probation reviews.
- Maintain accurate employee records, HR systems, spreadsheets and HR files.
- Produce HR correspondence, reports and management information.
- Support payroll administration and monitor employee lifecycle activities.
- Manage telephone and email enquiries professionally, including several busy inboxes.

About You:
We are looking for someone who can combine sound HR knowledge with excellent organisation, attention to detail and a willingness to support high-volume administrative activity.

You will ideally have:
- A minimum of three years' experience in an HR Assistant or HR Administration role, with this being your current or most recent position.
- Experience supporting employee relations matters, including absence, disciplinary, grievance and probation processes.
- Basic knowledge of UK employment law, including redundancy consultation and TUPE principles.
- Experience drafting HR correspondence, meeting invitations, outcome letters and manager scripts.
- Confidence advising and constructively challenging managers when appropriate.
- Experience using an HR information system, ideally People First or a similar platform.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information professionally.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Strong attention to detail and a process-driven approach.

Knowledge of HR best practice, further employee relations experience and a full UK driving licence would also be beneficial.
Why Apply?
This is an excellent opportunity to join a busy HR function and gain exposure to a broad range of employee relations, recruitment and HR operational activity. The role would suit an experienced HR Assistant who can quickly build relationships, confidently support managers and balance advisory work with essential HR administration.

If you are available at short notice and meet the essential requirements, please apply with an up-to-date CV for further information.

title: Centre Coordinator
description:
The Centre Co-ordinator will be responsible for the day-to-day management of the centre, for co-ordinating the planning and delivery of activities, services and events and for our team of centre volunteers.
Working closely with the Treasurer and Trustees, the Co-ordinator will ensure that the centre is maintained as a well-run, welcoming place for local people of all ages, and that it delivers activities to achieve the key outcomes identified in the workplan to be agreed with Trustees.
In the first year in post the Co-ordinator will be expected to strengthen and support our activities for children, young people, families and older people in line with current funding targets.

The role involves engaging with our funding partners, trustees, staff and volunteers and key elements are:

Community Development

This will involve building relationships with community members and with other community agencies and organisations and use the centre to strengthen community relationships.We would expect you to consult with centre users and community members to identify their needs and plan activities and services to meet those needsThe role may involve setting up and growing new clubs and groups to meet the needs of different groups in the village and supporting and encouraging community volunteers to set up community groups and activities which meet specific needs in the village, and provide space for these within the centre.

Centre and Volunteer Management

You must be able to deal professionally with enquiries made by community members, partner agencies and other community organisations either in person, by phone, by e-mail or by other means with regard to use of the Centre and its facilities including, with other staff, taking room bookings including payments and issuing of receipts and to ensure that an accurate bookings diary is maintained.Working with key holders to ensure that arrangements are in place for opening and closing the centre and for preparing the Centre for use. Working with our cleaner to ensure the Centre is clean and well maintained Volunteers are very important and we would need you to support the recruitment, selection and training of new volunteers and support current volunteers.

You would need to ensure that all policies and procedures are up to date, implemented and followed and to train and delegate the day to day responsibility for health and safety to staff and volunteers as appropriate.

Fundraising and Financial Management

We would support you to identify funding sources and streams and, with the agreement of the Treasurer, to draft funding bids to secure funding for current and new activities and projects, as well as ongoing core/revenue/capital costs. You would be responsible for properly maintaining the Centre's monitoring and evaluation processes to ensure data can be collected and collated to provide robust evidence to support funding bids, preparing reports requested by funders e.g. progress reports, end of grant reports and to work with the trustees to review funding needs and to agree fundraising targets and plans. Also you would work with volunteers and staff to plan fundraising activities and events to generate unrestricted funding to support Centre running costs and activities and work with the Treasurer to manage the Centre's finances, including responsibility for: Payments and receipts; Day to day small scale expenditure; Petty cash; Invoices; Records of income and expenditure; Volunteer and other expenses; Spending in relation to specific grants restricted funding . Your support would help the Treasurer with the production of financial reports for Trustees.

Partnership Working

We would want you to establish, maintain and grow relationships with local voluntary and statutory sector partner organisations and agencies near us, attend network and partnership meetings as agreed with the Treasurer., identify opportunities for collaborative approaches and joint funding bids with relevant partners and ensure partnership agreements are in place for funded work

Publicity and Promotion

With other staff and volunteers you would ensure that the Centre's website and social media accounts are regularly updated, provide information about Centre activities via local newsletter/s and social media, circulate information via email networks and partner organisations and be aware regular groups in the Centre ensuring they have information about upcoming activities and new developments.
